articles.title: FIFA Accuses European Body UEFA of 'Smear Campaign' in Filing Related to World Cup Sell-Off Plan
articles.summary: FIFA accused European soccer body UEFA of a "smear campaign" in a court filing on Thursday concerning FIFA President Gianni Infantino's failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup and other competitions.
articles.body:
FIFA accused European soccer body UEFA of a "smear campaign" in a court filing on Thursday concerning FIFA President Gianni Infantino's failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup and other competitions.

Last week, UEFA filed requests for discovery of evidence connected to Infantino's proposal in three U.S. courts.

"While these applications are styled as legal pleadings with captions and docket numbers, they are little more than press releases in further support of UEFA's smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership," FIFA said in a filing in U.S. District Court in Colorado.

FIFA's filing in Colorado on Thursday was a motion to intervene, asking that the discovery process be deferred or dropped.

One of UEFA's discovery requests was filed in the Southern District of New York and seeks disclosure of documents from Josh Kushner and his investment firm Thrive Capital Management. Kushner is the younger brother of Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump's son-in-law.

Thrive was involved in Infantino's FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup to private equity for $4.2 billion. FIFA withdrew the proposal on Aug. 1, just days after it was made public, after intense pushback.

Other court filings seeking discovery of evidence related to the World Cup sell-off were filed in Florida, where FIFA had its 2026 World Cup operational base, and in Colorado, against an adviser to Infantino, Greg Maffei, once the CEO of Liberty Media.

In a statement Monday to the outlet Axios , Kushner defended the proposal but said he did not anticipate the pushback.

"While we stand behind the motivations of FFE, we failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football, and the lengths some would go to. Thrive has a long track record of being a partner to all constituents. Had we known what this would devolve into, we would not have gotten involved," the statement said.

Kushner also agreed last month to purchase the NBA's Los Angeles Lakers with partner Bob Iger.

UEFA has said in court documents that it is preparing a criminal complaint against Infantino in Swiss courts for possible financial mismanagement.

"Infantino claimed that the plan would 'unleash the commercial potential and opportunity that FIFA has,'" UEFA lawyers told the courts. "In truth, it was a vehicle for Infantino and that small circle to acquire a permanent stake in and otherwise profit from FIFA's most valuable assets to the detriment of FIFA, its members, and other parties within the football family."

FIFA argued that UEFA's request "suffers from a fundamental defect: UEFA seeks discovery in aid of a foreign criminal proceeding that does not exist and that UEFA admittedly lacks the authority to initiate."

In the filing, FIFA accused UEFA of coercing its European federations to oppose the plan.

articles.title: Jerry Sandusky's Lawyers Want to Put Off Accuser's Recantation Hearing in a Bid for a New Trial
articles.summary: STATE COLLEGE, Pa. (AP) — Lawyers for former Penn State assistant football coach Jerry Sandusky asked Thursday to cancel a court date for a hearing over a claim that an accuser wants to recant allegations that Sandusky sexually abused him years ago.
articles.body:
STATE COLLEGE, Pa. (AP) — Lawyers for former Penn State assistant football coach Jerry Sandusky asked Thursday to cancel a court date for a hearing over a claim that an accuser wants to recant allegations that Sandusky sexually abused him years ago.

The hearing was scheduled for Sept. 8 in the latest bid by Sandusky's lawyers to secure a new trial for him. The judge in the case scheduled a status conference Friday to discuss it with defense lawyers, who suggested in a court filing that they want first to appeal the judge's refusal to hear other claims besides the accuser's recantation.

NCAA Clears Cincinnati in Sorsby Investigation

Sandusky, 82, has been serving a decades-long prison sentence since he was convicted of 45 counts of sexual abuse in 2012, after eight young men testified about what happened to them as boys. He has repeatedly lost efforts to get a new trial.

The Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General has said that the supposed recantation is "highly suspect."

The accuser, identified in court documents as R.R., said he was coached extensively by authorities.

"I was told — both directly and indirectly — that trauma may have fragmented my memory, and that I could safely affirm details I did not fully recall. I was assured this was common and even expected," R.R. said in an affidavit filed by Sandusky's attorneys.

R.R.'s allegations were "based on suggestive leading questioning, prosecutorial coercion and influence, confirmatory bias and memory manipulation, which permeated throughout each of the accusers as well," the defense said.

Sandusky was the defensive coordinator at one of the country's top football programs under Hall of Fame head coach Joe Paterno. The scandal led to Paterno's firing, and the university paid more than $100 million to people who said they were abused by Sandusky.

Authorities said he found and groomed boys at The Second Mile, a charity he founded for at-risk youth. Sandusky has repeatedly declared his innocence .

R.R., who was 25 years old at trial, testified that when he was 11, Sandusky sexually abused him in the coach's basement in 1998, a transcript shows.

"He told me that if I told anybody that I would never see my family again," said R.R., who was in foster care at the time.

Sandusky later apologized and said "he loved me," R.R. testified.

articles.title: LSU's 'test of the system' just the latest byproduct of a broken college sports world — 'It's embarrassing'
articles.summary: There is no clear, easy route to stability in college sports. There is no single leader to move the industry forward. It's lost in a quagmire of its own maki...
articles.body:
As a plaintiff attorney cross-examined SEC commissioner Greg Sankey on the witness stand in a Louisiana courtroom Thursday afternoon, news broke that his conference had filed a lawsuit against one of his own members.

If you're keeping tabs, this is the second time that a league filed a legal challenge against its own school in the last couple of months (the SEC's suit, in fact, is similar to the one the Big 12 filed against Texas Tech to prevent the school from playing QB Brendan Sorsby ). The SEC's lawsuit happened a few weeks after a group of players, some recruited by LSU and who already signed pro contracts, sued the SEC over an additional year of eligibility in a Louisiana court .

In an era of college athletics boiling over in legal jambalaya, this is only the tip of the proverbial iceberg. Let's take inventory of the insanity.

Just in the last three years, four schools have filed lawsuits against another school or their own player (for buyouts and tortious interference); a group of players or an individual player has twice sued their coach (broken NIL promises); and a conference has sued another conference or one of their member schools at least nine different times (mostly over realignment).

One power league athletic director summed it up quite nicely on Thursday.

"At this point, you got to wonder what people are thinking about our industry," he said. "It's embarrassing."

College sports remains mired in the worst kind of purgatory. The industry wobbles erratically, caught between the old amateurism model and full-blown professionalism. Its stakeholders disagree on a way forward. Do you push back against mounting legal challenges with conference-wide restrictions? Or lunge forward into a more pro scheme through collective bargaining?

There is a group, too, still stacking their eggs in the congressional basket, hoping for a federal bill to regulate the industry — something that took a hit on Thursday morning, when House leaders announced they would end their September session two weeks earlier than expected (even if the Senate passes the Protect College Sports Act when it returns to session on Sept. 15, the House would not consider it until mid-November).

All three paths forward seem murky and rife with obstacles.

There is no clear, easy route to stability. There is no single leader to move the industry forward.

However, the power conferences took a large step last week down the road toward conference-wide governance by creating/reaffirming policies on banning pro players returning to college (a response to players' legal pursuit in the Louisiana case). In theory, individual leagues would create and enforce rules among a smaller cohort to avoid the antitrust litigation that's crippled the NCAA and its rules.

Will it work? The SEC's aggressive approach to the LSU situation is a clear sign that the league believes it must vigorously defend its conference rules or else risk the collapse of any league-wide governance concept before it's even established.

Sankey himself took it seriously enough to appear in court.

In an act indicative of the current state of the industry, the SEC commissioner spent more than three hours of the first week of the football season on the stand testifying during a preliminary injunction hearing over the eligibility of several professional football players wanting to return to college.

What's going down in Baton Rouge is a product of a broken system.

Blame the longtime executives of the industry who, for years, ignored the obvious economic inequity in player compensation. Blame the school administrators and coaches who are intentionally breaking the very rules that they create. Blame plaintiff attorneys who rake in big bucks while preaching colleges' mistreatment of athletes.

Blame the media, which mostly stood by idly for decades while power conference universities used the profits of football to overspend on money-losing Olympic sports, coaching and administrator salaries, and gaudy facilities.

"I'm indicting everyone, including myself," said Kevin White, an athletic director at six different NCAA schools over 40 years, at a Knight Commission meeting in 2023. "We should have been far more progressive and forward thinking over the past 20 years or more."

The current situation is dire enough that White believes the industry is approaching an "irreconcilable position between the academy and college athletics" — a nod toward the thinning tether that connects a university with a major football program.

That tether feels strained more than ever, stretched to the point of tearing.

While what's unfolding in Louisiana is the byproduct of an unhealthy system — half-amateur and half-professional — you'd be silly to believe that LSU doesn't deserve some fault for planning to break the very rules that its university president voted on just last week (professional players should be prohibited from returning to college).

According to the SEC's federal lawsuit against the school, LSU and coach Lane Kiffin "orchestrated a campaign to recruit professional athletes" to join the roster this year. The suit takes aim at university president Wade Rousse, his school board and athletic director, Verge Ausberry, for permitting Kiffin to pursue ineligible players.

"Someone has to test the system," said one high-ranking LSU administrator earlier this week.

LSU's antics sparked public condemnation from a slew of southern state attorneys general. Georgia's AG, Chris Carr, encouraged Sankey to expel the school from the league if it rosters pro players — a move that, while extreme, has been discussed among the 15 SEC university presidents, as reported Monday at Yahoo . South Carolina's attorney general, Alan Wilson, believes that the league should be able to enforce its rules as a private association.

Louisiana's attorney general clapped back, as did the state's governor, Jeff Landry, who many believe to be in support of LSU's pursuit of these players.

College sports stands at an impasse. Kickoff can't get here soon enough.

articles.title: WSL 2026/27 transfer window winners and losers: Ecstatic Arsenal, but have Man City and Chelsea done enough?
articles.summary: The 2026/27 WSL season kicks off on Friday night as London City Lionesses host Manchester United, live on Sky Sports Football from 6pm; kick-off 7pm; the transfer window shut on Thursday night - who were the winners and losers from a busy summer's business?
articles.body:
Manchester City managed to keep hold of FWA Women's Footballer of the Year Bunny Shaw, but have the champions done enough business to retain their title?

Meanwhile, Chelsea and Manchester United head into the new campaign with questions over whether they have strengthened enough to be challenging for the title, in contrast to West Ham and Tottenham Hotspur, who have both enjoyed eye-catching summers.

So, as the WSL transfer window finally slams shut for business, we look at the winners and losers from the summer with the new season set to get under way on Friday Night when London City host Man Utd live on Sky Sports .

Arsenal & London City winners of the window

If the answer to the question 'Who has improved most this window?' isn't Arsenal or London City, then they need to have a word with their recruitment teams.

Elisa De Almeida is Arsenal's eighth new signing and most of the players brought in are at a point in their career they're supposed to be at their peak.

Big things are expected of Georgia Stanway , Ona Batlle , Geraldine Reuteler and others as the club looks to win their first WSL title since 2019.

As for London City - another sixth-placed finish after their star-studded signing drive won't be tolerated.

Arsenal are ecstatic with their window, they feel as though they have a squad ready to take on all comers.

Georgia Stanway, Ona Batlle, Misa Rodriguez, Selina Cerci and Elisa De Almeida are expected to raise standards and help Arsenal get over the hump, and Renee Slegers is already chuffed with the impact they're making at London Colney.

The club's really high on Lisa Baum's potential, she's been turning heads in training.

They also have Katie Reid and Michelle Agyemang to come back before the end of the year, which means the future's bright.

Summer signings have quality to make London City contenders

It should pay off [London City's summer spending]. They've signed the favourite for this year's Ballon d'Or (Alexia Putellas), a Champions League-winning centre-back (Mapi Leon) and a goalkeeper once named the best in the world (Mary Earps).

Regardless of age, these players have the quality and character to make London City contenders.

You can argue it's an old squad, you can argue there's a lot of pressure to click quickly and you can argue whether the coach has the big-game and big-name experience, but talent-wise, it's one heck of a squad.

Some pundits have them as title challengers, some as top-three entrants and some as major disappointments.

The fun is in seeing how this plays out.

Former England international Jill Scott:

Whenever we speak about the big teams, we always say how important it is to have a good goalkeeper.

And having Mary Earps back in the WSL, she's going to be great for them.

There's a lot of experience in that team and you speak about Alexia Putellas in that team - they'll definitely be up there.

Questions being asked about whether Man City have done enough business

Manchester City are not starting the season how they want to.

They're dealing with some injuries to some key players, including Vivianne Miedema , Jade Rose , Grace Clinton and Sydney Lohmann .

It's why they made a move for Joe Echegini and signed Carlotta Wamser late in the window.

Signing two players in Beth Mead and Niamh Charles adds to their pool of experience, but with the return of Champions League football, questions are being asked about whether enough has been done this summer.

For me, Man City are still title favourites and a big reason for that is by keeping hold of Bunny Shaw .

Her goal record speaks for itself and having Beth Mead in the squad now supplying her with more goals, I'd still go for City.

United fans must brace themselves for a new reality

Manchester United fans need to brace themselves for a new reality.

The club has changed its ethos, as well as its head coach. Eva Olid has been brought in to usher a new generation of players at United, which means they may have different short-term aims compared to previous seasons.

Saying that, they did shell out around £700k at the end of the window to sign Sweden winger Monica Jusu Bah and Rebecca Bernal , with the former bringing pace and excitement and the latter experience and grit.

It's what happens next that's the big test of their ambitions. Ella Toone is in the last year of her contract.

Chelsea were expected to go bigger this summer after looking flat last season

We all expected Chelsea to go bigger this summer and it's not as though they didn't try.

A league-leading contract was offered to Bunny Shaw , who opted to stay at Manchester City at the last moment.

A potential world-record fee was offered for Sweden striker Felicity Schroder , but she decided to move to Real Madrid.

Bringing Katie McCabe and Melvine Malard's experience and dynamism is a positive to a side that looked flat last season.

The club's really high on the signings of youngsters Giulia Dragoni and Manaka Matsukubo , who could have a bigger impact than expected.

Spurs and West Ham's eye-catching off-season?

How can you not be impressed with Spurs? Caitlin Dijkstra brings UWCL experience, Kirsty Hanson had a brilliant season at Aston Villa, Shekiera Martinez should add more goals and Alice Sombath won Europe's biggest competition at Lyon.

They'll be eyeing up at least fourth place this season.

West Ham are another club that's really happy with their off-season. Kelly Gago never got going at Everton, but she's an exciting striker that could light up East London.

Ebony Salmon's looking to live up to her early promise at a new club and Laia Codina brings a World Cup-winners' medal to the changing room.

Can they make the leap? A good test is Spurs away in Week One.

Putellas is the biggest signing the league has seen

Alexia Putellas is the biggest signing the league has seen and the results will be felt in many ways.

London City have sold out their home stadium in Bromley for the first time as people are desperate to see her debut.

Major brands are more likely to see LCL and the WSL as an attractive prospect as Putellas is one of the few global faces of women's football.

Putellas' experience as a four-time UWCL winner and World Cup winner, as well as her veracious attitude for success, has already had an impact at London City training. But on the pitch is where it matters.

Putellas is confident she can bring her world-class talent to the WSL week after week, which is an exciting prospect.

No WSL player has ever won the Ballon d'Or - Putellas hopes her start of season form with her new club will cement her case to end that drought.

Watch London City vs Man Utd live on Sky Sports Football from 6pm on Friday, kick-off 8pm. Follow across Sky Sports digital platforms and watch in-game clips and free match highlights shortly after full time.

articles.title: UNC's Michael Lombardi resigns as investigation reportedly includes questions about Steve Belichick
articles.summary: Lombardi had been on paid leave since July. Investigators are reportedly asking questions about accusations of drug use by Belichick, as well as inquiring ab...
articles.body:
Michael Lombardi is out at North Carolina amid the school's internal investigation.

The football program's general manager had been on paid leave as a result of that investigation. The school announced Lombardi's resignation Thursday afternoon and said the investigation continued. Lombardi came to North Carolina when the school hired former New England Patriots coach Bill Belichick after the 2024 season.

"Effective September 3, 2026, Michael Lombardi has resigned from his position as General Manager of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill's football program," the school's statement said. "The University will continue its ongoing investigation and will consider all appropriate corrective actions responsive to the information it learns."

According to a report from WRAL that was released shortly after Lombardi's resignation became public, there are multiple facets to the inquiry. One of the topics includes questions surrounding potential alleged drug use by North Carolina defensive coordinator Steve Belichick, Bill's son.

Steve Belichick is currently on medical leave for undisclosed reasons. He also came to North Carolina when his father was hired. From WRAL:

Lawyers hired to conduct the investigation are also questioning people about whether defensive coordinator Steve Belichick used drugs on the job or provided drugs to at least one player — and, separately, about whether a member of UNC's recruiting staff had a sexual relationship with a player, people familiar with the investigation told WRAL. They also asked about possible sexual relationships between assistant coaches and recruiting staff, the people said.

The investigation also reportedly encompasses questions about accusations involving a sexual relationship between a recruiting staffer and "at least one" North Carolina player along with "similar possible relationships" between recruiting staff and assistant coaches.

In a statement through attorney Tom Mars to WRAL after his resignation, Lombardi said that he resigned so that the team could focus on the season. His resignation came less than a week after Mars said that North Carolina's investigation was a "witch hunt."

"If UNC had grounds to fire Michael for cause, they wouldn't need to conduct such a far-ranging, lengthy witch hunt. They would have done so by now," attorney Tom Mars said. "I think the motive behind the investigation goes further than a $1.5 million buyout. After all, UNC could fire Michael (or the athletic director or any head coach) for no reason at all just by paying their buyout. In today's world, $1.5 million is just a drop in the bucket, so there must be other reasons behind this multimillion-dollar investigation."

Lombardi's salary of $1.5 million made him the highest-paid general manager in college football. He was in the second season of a three-year deal.

He first worked with Belichick when the two were with the Cleveland Browns in the late 1980s and then worked with Belichick again in New England. The 67-year-old was an "assistant to the coaching staff" from 2014 through 2016 before working in media ahead of Belichick's hire at North Carolina.

Steve Belichick also previously worked for his father before coming to North Carolina. The 39-year-old was an assistant with the Patriots from 2012 through 2023 and spent the 2024 season as Washington's defensive coordinator. After a season with the Huskies, he came to Chapel Hill to run UNC's defense.

According to WRAL's report, people are being asked if they had seen or knew of anyone who had seen Steve Belichick use drugs at North Carolina's facilities.

The wide-ranging investigation is the latest — and biggest — issue for a North Carolina program that has dealt with numerous headlines that have nothing to do with the team's play on the field.

Bill Belichick's relationship with girlfriend Jordon Hudson has drawn a lot of attention, especially after the way the two refused to address questions about the beginning of their relationship in a CBS interview last year. After the interview, Belichick said that Hudson, who also operates as a personal public relations manager for the coach, was simply "doing her job" to keep the interview on topic.

In the middle of last season, assistant coach Armond Hawkins was suspended after he allegedly provided extra sideline passes to a player's family.

And at the beginning of his tenure, Lombardi said that he wanted to consider North Carolina the 33rd team of the NFL. The Tar Heels were overmatched all season and went 4-8.

The 2026 season has started better on the field, however. The Tar Heels got a 15-10 victory over TCU in Dublin in Week 0. The game was a rematch from the teams' season-opener a year ago, where TCU drubbed the Tar Heels after much fanfare for Belichick's first home game at North Carolina.

UNC is off in Week 1 ahead of a game against East Tennessee State in Week 2.

articles.title: How Michigan Football QB Bryce Underwood is ‘dialed in’ ahead of season opener
articles.summary: Here’s why Michigan offensive coordinator Jason Beck says QB Bryce Underwood is dialed in ahead of the season opener vs. Western Michigan.
articles.body:
Not many quarterbacks are talked about more nationally than Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood — for better and worse. That comes with the territory of being the No. 1 overall recruit in the 2025 class and starting for Michigan as a true freshman. Underwood went 9-4 as a starter last year, and threw for 11 touchdowns with nine interceptions along with six rushing scores.

"I think the expectations might have been a little high for him last year," new Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham said. "I mean, he was a just-turned-18-year-old true freshman and thrust into the starting role of the Michigan Wolverines. And, you know, I don't know what people did expect, but he was able to win nine ball games and put up some decent numbers. I mean, he knows, we know that those numbers have to improve."

There are certainly heightened expectations for Underwood heading into his sophomore campaign. He has a new offensive coordinator in Jason Beck and a scheme that will allow Underwood to use his legs more and also allow plenty of chances through the air. Underwood also has offensive weapons to help him succeed — most notably wideouts like Andrew Marsh and JJ Buchanan and running backs in Jordan Marshall and Savion Hiter.

Underwood has improved since the beginning of the offseason. He had a new scheme to learn on top of refining his mechanics. A lot was thrown at Underwood. Michigan quarterbacks coach Koy Detmer Jr. said that a lot was thrown at Underwood and he "really worked his tail off." From learning a new system to improving his footwork and pocket presence, Detmer said that things have been moving slower for Underwood in fall camp.

When speaking with the media on Wednesday, Jason Beck talked about Underwood's journey this offseason. With Michigan's season opener just two days away versus Western Michigan, it sounds as if Underwood is in a good place.

"With spring, everything was so new that there were really good days and there were bad days," Beck said . "It was really more up and down, where throughout this fall camp it's been much more steady, much more consistent, much more predictable day in, day out with those reads and decisions and the quickness of those decisions. So he made a really nice jump that you'd hope would happen from spring to fall with just a better understanding, more decisive, more dialed in with everything that's happening."

Beck said that Underwood took a reall big jump from spring to fall camp, something that Whittingham mentioned earlier this week, calling Underwood "markedly better through fall camp than he was at any point in spring."

It's been a busy offseason for Underwood, who didn't take much time off. Underwood worked out with quarterback trainer Jordan Palmer this summer. Underwood spent time training side by side with Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow. Underwood said in July that "staying calm through the storm" like Burrow is something he's working on. Underwood may have done all the right things this offseason to put him in the best situation to succeed once the games start to count, and now it's time to see if his labor has fruitful rewards.

articles.title: Is Hearts' McPake poised to gatecrash Pocognoli's Scotland squad?
articles.summary: Josh McPake has made a significant impact since joining Hearts. Could he now do the same for the Scotland national team?
articles.body:
On the eve of the Scottish FA's highly-anticipated summit on youth development in Scotland, one of the country's own stole the show in a thrilling Edinburgh derby.

And as it happened, the new national team head coach, Sebastien Pocognoli, was in the Easter Road stands as Josh McPake spearheaded Hearts' entertaining victory over Hibernian.

Even before the Belgian was appointed, there were some calls from the Tartan Army to include the 25-year-old winger, such has been his emphatic start to life in Gorgie since making the switch from St Johnstone in the summer.

The clamour for his inclusion is now becoming inescapable.

A Rangers youth product, the question hanging over McPake since signing his pre-contract with Hearts in January, was could he cut it among the big boys.

Under the lights in Leith, McPake waltzed through the weak Hibs backline before bending a beautiful effort beyond Raphael Sallinger - with a deflection off Grant Hanley - sparking bedlam among the travelling supporters behind the goal.

Thrilling Hearts earn Edinburgh derby win over 10-man Hibs

Latest Hearts news, analysis and fan views

Get Hearts news notifications in the BBC Sport app

The talk of the toon are the boys in maroon, but the chat in all corners of the country is about McPake. He really is the man of the moment.

In eight games, he has registered two goals and four assists for an increasingly easy-on-the-eye Hearts side, who are emerging as contenders for the campaign's great entertainers.

In the first 30 minutes at the home of their city rivals, they were magnificent. McPake - along with fellow Scotland hopeful Calvin Miller - was unplayable, hugging the touchline and leaving home full-back Felix Passlack for dust.

He destroyed the former Borussia Dortmund defender before teeing up James Wilson's opener, with former Hearts striker Ryan Stevenson explaining that was the perfect example of how much of a handful he is.

"It is so hard for defenders when wingers play on the opposite side," Stevenson said on Sportsound. "They always want to come on the inside, but he is happy to go on the outside and feint and go on his left side.

"One of his biggest attributes is you don't know which way he will go."

That was evident again when McPake took a stroll for his superb solo goal, one he was desperate for in his first derby.

"I thought we started the game really, really well," McPake told BBC Sport Scotland. "Obviously, I got the assist in the first half, but I really, really wanted the goal."

While he was happy to admit his desire to get on the scoresheet, the winger was a little more reluctant to indulge in any Scotland call-up conversation.

As understandable and mature as that may be, it won't stop the rest of us doing so. But McPake is more reserved than most because of his tricky route to the top.

After coming through the Rangers ranks, he was sent out on loan six times, before finally settling at Stirling Albion in League 1.

Impressing, he caught the eye of St Johnstone, albeit he was initially involved in their top-flight relegation.

It was in the second-tier last term where McPake started to shine. Head and shoulders above the rest, Derek McInnes' Hearts secured his services on a pre-contract. Then McInnes left Tynecastle for Ibrox.

"These things happen in football," explained McPake, who couldn't hide his appreciation for Vrancken.

Are Hearts derby heroes ready for Scotland?

That feeling is reciprocated. Even if the attacker was left out of Hearts initial European squad.

"It was a difficult start and he had to adapt in several ways and the things we wanted to see and be decisive in certain moments," the head coach said.

"But he did great and picked up those things and he is really strong in defence as well as offence and I'm pleased to see this happening."

And it appears Vrancken isn't the only one, with the winger dominating much of the post-match discussions.

"I know he has had loan moves, but it is about getting the right environment and the right manager," former Hibs midfielder Scott Allan said on Sportsound.

"Now he has landed with Wouter Vrancken and I think he will be a manager who will enhance his career.

"When they get him isolated, he puts defenders under pressure.

"I wouldn't be surprised if he is named in the next Scotland squad because he is the standout at present."

While McPake might be the standout, he has a more than decent support act.

Fellow forwards Miller and Wilson are in the mix for involvement in the upcoming Nations League games this month, too.

Teenager Wilson has already been capped, but since spending the second half of last season on loan with Tottenham Hotspur's under-21 side, he has taken his game up a notch.

His second derby goal at Easter Road will have done his hopes of a national team return no harm - nor will his wonderstrike against Rapid Vienna - with Stevenson adding he showed "total striker's instinct".

"We have to come to the point with a new manager coming in for Scotland, there is room to bring in a bit of freshness," he added.

Not dominating the discourse as much as last week for his heroics in Austria, hirpling into the box to score in extra-time and force penalties before netting his own, Miller strengthened his case yet again for an impressive performance.

He was spoken off in some circles as an outside shout for a World Cup spot following his superb Falkirk form, but that always seemed too much of a stretch.

But now, he and his team-mates are front and centre, catching the eye of everyone watching. Mr Pocognoli, are you watching?

articles.title: FIFA accuses UEFA of 'smear campaign' over investor plan
articles.summary: FIFA says legal applications made by UEFA to access documents related to FIFA's controversial private investor plan are part of a "smear campaign" against th...
articles.body:
FIFA says legal applications made by UEFA to access documents related to FIFA's controversial private investor plan are part of a "smear campaign" against the global governing body.

UEFA is applying through the American courts for discovery of evidence and documentation linked to FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a private company which it was envisaged would run the World Cup and other FIFA competitions.

FIFA confirmed last month the plan had been to sell a 20% stake in that company to private investors. The plan was withdrawn by FIFA president Gianni Infantino on August 1 amid opposition from UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and CONCACAF, the confederation for countries in North and Central America plus the Caribbean.

That withdrawal has not stopped UEFA pursuing Infantino and other FIFA officials, with UEFA saying documents obtained were intended for use in preparing potential criminal proceedings in Switzerland, in filings seen by the Press Association on August 27.

The following day, FIFA sought approval to oppose UEFA's request in the Southern District of Florida, a motion which was granted by the court on the next business day, August 31. FIFA has until September 28 to submit a full opposition to that court.

A similar motion to oppose was also filed in the Southern District of New York on Tuesday. Documents from FIFA's legal team seen by the Press Association describe UEFA's applications as being "little more than press releases in further support of UEFA's smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership."

FIFA's filing asks the New York court to defer consideration on UEFA's discovery application until the Florida court has ruled on it, or requests that the court permit FIFA permission to oppose UEFA's application no later than September 30.

The filing said UEFA's motivation in its opposition to FFE and Infantino was "to prevent smaller countries from having the financial strength to compete with the European elite."

It added: "If soccer is strengthened in the developing world, global competition increases, which ultimately reduces UEFA's market power and provides more competition for its flagship tournaments.

"By raising funds to allow some of FIFA's smaller member associations to better develop soccer, FFE would lead to more players from those nations choosing to represent their countries of origin and playing in their home leagues rather than playing abroad.

"All of this would erode UEFA's dominance over other regions of the world."

UEFA's filing accused Infantino of "criminal mismanagement" in relation to FFE, and said the proposed sale of a stake for $4.2 billion in the company was "a fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit."

In a separate statement published last week, UEFA called for an independent external review of the origins of the FFE and said that if Infantino chose to stand for re-election at next year's FIFA Congress, UEFA would "join forces with its partner confederations to ensure that member associations are offered a credible alternative - one committed to integrity, accountability, development and genuine institutional change."

articles.title: Lionel Messi gets new Inter Miami teammate who sparked huge backlash during World Cup
articles.summary: A new teammate has joined Lionel Messi at Inter Miami who created huge outrage among French football fans during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Midfield star Matia...
articles.body:
A new teammate has joined Lionel Messi at Inter Miami who created huge outrage among French football fans during the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Midfield star Matias Galarza of Paraguay has joined Inter Miami from Argentinian club River Plate on loan until the end of the 2026 season, with an option to buy.

Lionel Messi has a new teammate at Inter Miami

Inter Miami announced Galarza's acquisition via their X handle, writing:

"Paraguayan talent in Miami. Welcome, Matías!"

Galarza had a forgettable stint at River Plate after joining the team in 2025 from Talleres. Before that, he had played for Brazil's Vasco da Gama and Coritiba.

Galarza only made 14 appearances for River Plate and did not score a single goal, while managing just one assist. His performances prompted the club to send him on loan to Atlanta United in February 2026 before returning to River Plate.

Furthermore, Galarza made headlines during this year's FIFA World Cup when Paraguay faced France in the round of 16. He reportedly angered Les Bleus fans by deliberately provoking Kylian Mbappe and company to distract them from the game.

Notably, he clashed with French players such as Mbappe, Jules Kounde and Michael Olise, but France ended up winning the game 1-0.

Despite this, Galarza played a major role in Paraguay's 1-0 win over Turkey, scoring in the second minute to help Paraguay secure a place in the round of 16.

In 19 appearances for Paraguay, the 24-year-old has scored four goals and provided two assists.

articles.title: UMass Upsets Rutgers as Massive Underdogs, Snaps Longest Losing Streak in CFB, Final Box Score Stats
articles.summary: Led by a stellar performance from quarterback William Watson III, UMass pulled off a shocking 37-21 upset victory over Rutgers to begin the 2026 college football season at SHI Stadium on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Led by a stellar performance from quarterback William Watson III, UMass pulled off a shocking 37-21 upset victory over Rutgers to begin the 2026 college football season at SHI Stadium on Thursday night.

The Minutemen were able to secure the win despite entering the game as 28.5-point underdogs, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

UMass also snapped a 16-game losing streak on Thursday, as the team's last victory occurred in Oct. 2024.

Here's a look at Umass' stats as well as highlights from the game.

While Rutgers scored a touchdown on its opening possession, the Minutemen didn't waste any time before responding.

UMass found the end zone on each of its first three drives, highlighted by a 31-yard touchdown pass from Watson to Joseph Griffin Jr. that gave the team a 21-7 lead.

The Minutemen maintained a 24-7 edge at halftime.

While UMass slowed down offensively in the second half, head coach Joe Harasymiak's defense stepped up throughout the majority of the final two quarters.

Rutgers eventually cut the deficit to 16 points and had the ball with just over four minutes left in the game, although a UMass interception and subsequent Minutemen touchdown ended any hopes of a late comeback.

The Scarlet Knights finished with 349 total yards as a team, but committed four turnovers and converted just three of 11 opportunities on third down.

Meanwhile, UMass racked up 397 yards of offense without turning the ball over.

After posting an 0-12 record in 2025, the Minutemen are now 1-0 in 2026.

articles.title: Deion Sanders' Colorado Beats Georgia Tech in Wild Ending, Box Score, Top Player Stats & Highlights
articles.summary: For 58 minutes and 20 seconds, Georgia Tech and Colorado football played in a low-scoring rock fight in Atlanta.
articles.body:
For 58 minutes and 20 seconds, Georgia Tech and Colorado football played in a low-scoring rock fight in Atlanta.

That all changed in the final 100 seconds, which featured a frenetic finale.

Colorado emerged victorious 14-13 after (a) quarterback Julian Lewis found tight end Charlie Williams with a 20-yard touchdown pass with 37 seconds left and (b) Buffaloes defensive back Boo Carter blocked Georgia Tech's 45-yard field goal attempt as time ran out.

First look at Pro Bowler coaching for CFB team

Colorado got the ball back with 1:40 left in regulation on its own 25-yard line, down 13-7. Lewis got the Buffaloes moving with some big chunk plays, including passes to DeKalon Taylor for 17 yards and Joseph Williams for 16. Taylor also rushed for 16, leading to Charlie Williams' touchdown on a wheel route.

However, Georgia Tech immediately fired back as quarterback Alberto Mendoza found Dalen Penson for 42 yards on a crossing route. Then a couple of three-yard plays put the ball on the Colorado 27-yard line with three seconds left. Carter came through with the massive block, though, and Sanders' Buffaloes started the year with a huge win.

Both teams had first-quarter scoring chances but couldn't pull through. Georgia Tech kicker Aidan Birr missed a 35-yard field goal. Colorado then drove down the field and earned a 1st-and-goal at the Georgia Tech three-yard line.

The Yellow Jackets held firm, though, and forced a 4th-and-goal from the three. DeKalon Taylor's rush fell a yard short, though.

The Buffaloes then benefited from a short field after Colorado forced a three-and-out and then got the ball back on the Yellow Jackets' 35-yard line. Running back Micah Welch's five-yard touchdown ended the drive and opened the scoring.

However, Georgia Tech immediately responded when Rakheem Smith returned the kickoff 100 yards for a touchdown. Following the PAT, Georgia Tech and Colorado found themselves tied at seven.

Colorado drove to the Georgia Tech 40-yard line on its next drive but was forced to punt. The Yellow Jackets got pinned back again (this time on its own four-yard line) but engineered an impressive 92-yard drive that included five Alberto Mendoza complete passes for 83 yards. Aidan Birr's 22-yard field goal gave Georgia Tech the 10-7 lead with 2:03 left in the first half.

Both defenses stood tall in the scoreless third quarter, but Colorado got things going in the fourth as the Buffaloes ran 12 times for 39 yards, setting up a 38-yard field goal attempt. However, defensive tackle Shymeik Jones, who stands at 6'5", got up and blocked the kick.

Georgia Tech got the ball back on its own 21-yard line with 7:35 left and milked the clock for nearly six minutes, thanks in part to three third-down conversions, including two Mendoza passes to Jordan Allen (21 yards) and Kevin Roche Jr. (16 yards). The drive ended with Birr's second field goal, this time from 29 yards.

That led to a crazy finish, and Colorado ultimately emerged victorious. Lewis certainly deserves credit for his great play on the final drive, but credit goes to the defense as well, including defensive lineman Lamont Lester Jr., who had three sacks.

Both teams will now play at home on Saturday, Sept. 12. Colorado will face Weber State at 3:30 p.m. ET, and the Yellow Jackets will take on No. 20 Tennessee at 7 p.m.

articles.body: El F.C. Barcelona planea crear un parque de atracciones dentro de las instalaciones del Spotify Camp Nou. 'El Mundo Deportivo' informa que el Barça ha llegado a un acuerdo con Babylon Park Spain SL, y que el 19 de septiembre el club culé someterá a votación de los compromisarios el acuerdo para la concesión de parques infantiles para un plazo superior a los cinco años. Babylon Park es la red de parques temáticos de interior más avanzados del mundo a nivel tecnológico, con más de 20 recintos fuera de Europa y 30 años de experiencia. El concepto fue creado por Efi Malka, fundador de Babylon y Teddy Sagi, fundador de Playtech y propietario de Camden Market en Londres. Su primera flagship en España fue el Westfield Parquesur de Leganés (Madrid), que cuenta con la única montaña rusa interior en la Comunidad de Madrid. "En nuestra expansión en Europa, queremos apostar por el mercado español por su enorme potencial de crecimiento, debido a la cultura de ocio local. Estamos muy contentos de abrir nuestra primera flagship en España en Westfield Parquesur, el mayor centro comercial de Madrid y damos las gracias a Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield por ver en nosotros la oferta más atractiva de un concepto diferencial de entretenimiento familiar", explicaba en 2022 Nir Diamant, CEO de Babylon.

articles.title: Sergio Martínez, ascenso relámpago
articles.standfirst: El fichaje procedente del Racing de Santander, incorporado inicialmente al Castilla, ha entrenado dos días con el primer equipo y viajará convocado para el duelo liguero
articles.summary: El fichaje procedente del Racing de Santander, incorporado inicialmente al Castilla, ha entrenado dos días con el primer equipo y viajará convocado para el duelo liguero
articles.body: Sergio Martínez está viviendo un arranque de curso de vértigo. El futbolista, fichado hace apenas unos días por el Real Madrid procedente del Racing de Santander, ha pasado en un suspiro de la disciplina del filial a las puertas del primer equipo. Ya es uno más con los 'mayores'. Tras ejercitarse ayer con el grupo de Mourinho y repetir hoy en la sesión, el joven de Laredo entrará en la convocatoria para el partido ante el Real Betis, un salto tan inesperado como fulgurante, coronado con su inclusión en la lista A de la Champions League. El propio técnico confirmó la noticia en rueda de prensa, dejando claro que el chico entra en sus planes de forma progresiva. "El plan es que mañana esté en el banquillo, por ahí puedes ver más o menos cuál es el plan", explicó el luso. "Se ha entrenado con el primer equipo dos días, nada más". Una llamada que, sin ser aún la de un futbolista consolidado, supone un espaldarazo para un joven recién llegado. Mourinho quiso, además, poner en contexto la operación y su propia implicación en ella. "Antes de que el club lo fichara, y sabiendo que no sería directamente jugador para el primer equipo, analizamos y dimos nuestra opinión sobre si un día podría llegar aquí", desveló el portugués, que ya había avalado el potencial del jugador antes de su incorporación. El propio técnico subrayó las cualidades del joven, pero sin cargarle de presión en estos inicios de temporada. "Es un chico con potencial, que tiene una pequeña experiencia en la Segunda División y en este inicio de Liga con el Racing. Tiene que trabajar, y solo él lo podrá decir", advirtió. "La calidad y la intensidad aquí son diferentes, pero ahí está". Un mensaje que combina la confianza en sus condiciones con la exigencia propia de la casa. Conviene recordar de dónde viene este futbolista, formado íntegramente en el Racing, club al que perteneció desde los diez años y en el que escaló todos los peldaños hasta debutar en el fútbol profesional. Esta misma temporada se estrenó en Segunda con el conjunto verdiblanco, con el que llegó a marcar en la primera jornada liguera, un rendimiento que precipitó el interés del Madrid y su fichaje por unos tres millones de euros. Su presencia en la lista ante el Betis se enmarca, además, en la apuesta de Mourinho por la savia joven en este arranque de curso. "Mañana estará él, estará Rivas, que ya está desde el primer partido, y estará Cestero también. A ver si juega o no, pero es un paso estar ya con nosotros", zanjó el técnico. El de Laredo se suma así a la nómina de canteranos que el luso ha ido asomando al primer equipo, en una jornada que, juegue o no, quedará grabada en su memoria. Su llegada al Madrid es también un sueño del pasado. Nada nuevo para quien, años atrás, ya dejaba entrever su devoción por el club blanco en las redes sociales. Sergio Martínez lució durante un tiempo como foto de perfil la mítica imagen de Ancelotti celebrando la Liga de 2022 rodeado de Rodrygo, Alaba, Militao y Vinicius, y en su biografía mencionaba a Luka Modric en clara señal de idolatría hacia el croata. Detalles que hoy cobran otra dimensión, ahora que aquel niño racinguista comparte vestuario con los ídolos a los que admiraba desde la distancia.
